election_dates.primarySnippet: 25 P.S. § 2753(a): There shall be a General primary preceding each general election which shall be held on the third Tuesday of May in all even-numbered years, except in the year of the nomination of a President of the United States, in which year the General primary shall be held on the fourth Tuesday of April.
election_dates.generalSnippet: Pa. Const. art. VII, § 2 (General Election Day): The general election shall be held biennially on the Tuesday next following the first Monday of November in each even-numbered year, but the General Assembly may by law fix a different day, two-thirds of all the members of each House consenting thereto: Provided, That such election shall always be held in an even-numbered year.

state_background_check.value: No — Pennsylvania's constitution bars anyone convicted of embezzlement of public moneys, bribery, perjury, or other infamous crime from the General Assembly or from holding any office of trust or profit in the Commonwealth, but the U.S. Constitution's own qualifications for Congress (age, citizenship, residency) can't be added to by any state, so this doesn't reach U.S. House or Senate candidates
state_background_check.snippet: Pa. Const. art. II, § 7: "No person hereafter convicted of embezzlement of public moneys, bribery, perjury or other infamous crime, shall be eligible to the General Assembly, or capable of holding any office of trust or profit in this Commonwealth." Congressional qualifications are set exclusively by the U.S. Constitution, confirmed per https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/R41946.html: "the Framers intended the Constitution to be the exclusive source of qualifications for Members of Congress, and that the Framers thereby 'divested' States of any power to add qualifications."

civic_affiliations.snippet: I am honored to be the first woman elected to Pennsylvania s 6th Congressional District and the first Democrat since the Civil War, serving on the Armed Services Committee and the Select Committee on Intelligence. Learn more about me Representation Matters My experiences as a veteran, an educator, an entrepreneur, and an engineer give me a unique background to continue to meet the moment in our country s history and prepare for a better tomorrow. I believe in the inherent value of all people and that each of us has something to contribute. I believe in the Department of Defense and that diplomacy and our allies are integral to our national security. I believe that healthcare is a right, a living wage is necessary, climate change is urgent, and quality education enables people to live better lives. Fighting For You Serving as your representative in Washington, D.C. since 2019 has been a tremendous honor. I remain focused on transparency and accountability, and my voting record is publicly available. I m proud that I have won numerous awards, including the Democracy Award in three separate categories. However, as much as we have moved ahead and confronted many challenges, there s work to be done. That s why I co-founded the BIOTech Caucus to bring more good paying jobs and scientific innovation to our community and country. Also, I know many people are rightly concerned about the cost of everything. I am too, which is why I lead the New Dem Economic Growth and Cost of Living Working Group

bio_summary.value: As a third-generation veteran, service is the foundation of who I am. I earned my engineering degree from Stanford via an ROTC scholarship and later completed my M.S. in Technology and Policy at MIT. As a Captain in the USAFR, I served three years on active duty and thirteen in the Inactive Reserve. I was the COO of AND1 Basketball, co-founded B-Lab to promote B Corporations, and taught chemistry in North Philadelphia through Teach for America. For thirty years, my family and I have happily called Chester County our home. I am honored to be the first woman elected to Pennsylvania’s 6th Congressional District and the first Democrat since the Civil War, serving on the Armed Services Committee and the Select Committee on Intelligence.

bio_summary.value: Marty is a fourth-generation Pennsylvanian and a proud graduate of West Chester schools. His roots run deep — his great-grandfather helped establish Philadelphia's Chinatown as one of Pennsylvania's first Chinese immigrant families, and his mother immigrated from Portugal, taught in Philadelphia public schools, and then at West Chester East and Henderson High Schools as a substitute teacher. His father, a chemical engineer at DuPont and Westtown graduate, showed Marty that you work hard, give back, and leave things better for those who come next.
